scope: Final canonical disposition for CineGlobe's treaty/co-production dataset (38 stored treaties, 109 participant rows), reconciled at queue level (the only granularity both engines' outputs support).

summary.reconciliation_note: Codex structured the 38 stored treaties (109 participant rows) into 8 completion queues (4 x P0 major bilateral-list reconciliations: UK/Australia/Canada/France; 3 x P1 multilateral framework queues: European Convention, Eurimages, Ibermedia; 1 x P2 residual bilateral refresh) and closed ZERO of them with primary authority. Gemini independently assessed all 38 stored records in aggregate and found the majority (18 of 38) incorrect/stale, plus 5 missing material pathways beyond the stored 38 -- broadly corroborating that the treaty dataset is materially incomplete, though the two engines' outputs cannot be cross-checked treaty-by-treaty because neither produced a jointly addressable per-record key linking Gemini's current/stale call to a specific stored treaty row. Claude/Chat's own risk validation (this session, prior turn) independently confirmed via direct code inspection that Little Utopia's own treaty-coproduction path (Mauritius as anchor) is correctly evaluated against the REAL treaty_engine registry and PROVEN zero (no MU bilateral treaty, not an ECS signatory) -- this is a working, correct example of the consuming mechanism, not a defect; the gap is treaty DATA breadth (mostly non-MU treaties), not the mechanism that reads it.
summary.final_canonical_treaty_pathway_count_not: 38 stored treaty records remain the canonical starting inventory; 7 of 8 completion queues (covering the P0/P1 majority of those 38 plus multilateral frameworks) remain UNRESOLVED with zero closures, and Gemini's aggregate assessment independently found 18 of 38 stored records incorrect/stale plus 5 missing material pathways. A precise FINAL canonical treaty/pathway count cannot be stated with confidence until at minimum the 4 P0 bilateral-list queues (UK/AU/CA/FR) close -- this is one of the load-bearing reasons for the NO-GO gate result.

queue_dispositions.gemini_cross_check: Gemini's independent worldwide pass separately assessed all 38 stored treaties in aggregate (20 confirmed current / 18 incorrect-stale / 5 missing material pathways / 0 unresolved) but the underlying JSON does not carry a per-treaty status field, so per-record cross-validation against this queue's specific stored_records is not mechanically possible from what either engine produced. Not a conflict — a granularity gap.
